title: Saturn Could Float in a Bathtub 🪐 #shorts
description:
Saturn is so big that more than 700 Earths would fit inside it, yet its average density is only about 0.69 g/cm³ – roughly 70% of water. It is the only planet in our solar system less dense than water, so in a big enough bathtub it would (in theory) float. It also spins once every ~10.7 hours, and its rings are only about 10 metres thick in most places.

Sources: NASA, NASA/JPL, Encyclopaedia Britannica, Royal Museums Greenwich, Guinness World Records, Caltech IPAC Cool Cosmos, Universe Today

scenes.label: EARTHS INSIDE

scenes.text: Yet it only weighs about ninety five times as much as Earth.
That's because it's made mostly of hydrogen and helium, the lightest gases there are.
Its average density is only about zero point seven grams per cubic centimeter. Water is one.
scenes.label: WATER IS 1.00

scenes.text: It's the only planet in our solar system lighter than water.
And it spins fast. A whole day on Saturn lasts only about ten point seven hours.
The twist? Its famous rings are hundreds of thousands of kilometers across, but in most places only about ten meters thick.
